steps: A system is a group of interrelated components that work together to achieve a common goal.
The basic components of a system are input, processing, output, and feedback.
Input is the data or material entered into the system.
Processing changes the input into useful results.
Output is the result produced by the system.
Feedback provides information about the output and helps control or improve the system.
items.finalAnswer: A system is a group of interrelated components that work together through input, processing, output, and feedback.

steps: Natural systems occur in nature and are not made by humans.
Examples of natural systems are the solar system and the human body.
Artificial systems are designed and made by humans to achieve a specific purpose.
Examples of artificial systems are a computer system and a transportation system.
items.finalAnswer: Natural systems occur in nature, while artificial systems are designed and made by humans.

steps: The main components of a computer system are hardware, software, data, users, and procedures.
Hardware consists of the physical parts of a computer, such as the keyboard, monitor, and processor.
Software is a set of programs and instructions that tells the hardware what to do.
Data is the raw facts and figures processed by the computer.
Users are the people who operate or use the computer system.
Procedures are the rules and instructions for using the computer system.
items.finalAnswer: A computer system consists of hardware, software, data, users, and procedures.

steps: Personal computers are designed for use by one person for everyday tasks; desktop and laptop computers are examples.
Mobile computing systems are portable devices that can be used while moving; smartphones and tablets are examples.
Servers provide services, resources, or data to other computers over a network.
Mainframe computers process large amounts of data and support many users at the same time.
Supercomputers perform extremely complex calculations at very high speed.
Embedded systems are built into other devices and perform specific tasks, such as controlling a washing machine.
items.finalAnswer: Types of computing systems include personal computers, mobile systems, servers, mainframes, supercomputers, and embedded systems.

steps: The main components of the Von Neumann architecture are the Central Processing Unit (CPU), memory, and input/output devices.
The CPU consists of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), the Control Unit (CU), and registers.
The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
The Control Unit directs and coordinates the activities of the computer.
Memory stores data and instructions.
Input devices enter data and instructions, while output devices present the results.
items.finalAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture consists of the CPU (ALU, Control Unit, and registers), memory, and input/output devices.

steps: The Von Neumann architecture is a computer design in which data and instructions are stored in the same memory.
The CPU fetches instructions and data from memory, processes them, and stores the results.
Its key components are the CPU, memory, and input/output devices.
The CPU contains the ALU, Control Unit, and registers.
items.finalAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture stores data and instructions in the same memory and uses the CPU, memory, and input/output devices.

steps: Fetch: The Control Unit retrieves an instruction from memory.
Decode: The Control Unit interprets the instruction.
Execute: The CPU performs the operation specified by the instruction.
Store: The result is stored in memory or a register.
items.finalAnswer: The four steps of the instruction cycle are fetch, decode, execute, and store.

steps: The Von Neumann bottleneck is the limitation on the speed of data transfer between the CPU and memory.
Data and instructions share the same pathway between the CPU and memory.
As a result, the CPU may have to wait while data or instructions are transferred.
items.finalAnswer: The Von Neumann bottleneck is the limited transfer speed between the CPU and memory because they share the same pathway.
